subject: prd/feature-brainstorm
statement: While interviewing a human decision principal (the human realization of FR-4 — FR-16), the skill shall present every question turn in the principal's register rather than the record's: the question phrased in plain language with every house term or corpus anchor glossed inline (never a bare `F-n`/`D-n`/document reference), grounded in one concrete example — looked up from the corpus, code, or prior records where one exists, marked hypothetical otherwise, or replaced by an explicit `no example: <reason>` line when no illustrative case exists — and carrying an enumerated option set in which every option states its outcome on that same example (outcomes pairwise distinct, the FR-4 recommendation marked among them), or one to two sample answers with their meaning where the question is open-form; the record keeps its own register (NFR-2) untouched.
rationale: a question the principal cannot cheaply parse is answered by laborious decoding or by rubber-stamping the recommendation (R3), hollowing the G3 experience the stage exists to protect; one example threaded through every option makes the options comparable — same scenario, divergent endings — and an interviewer that cannot instantiate its options on a concrete case does not yet understand its own question (operator ruling 2026-07-30)
fit_criterion: across the fixture corpus, 100% of human-principal question turns carry the form — plain-language question, example or typed skip, enumerated options each stating its outcome on the turn's example (or sample answers for open-form), recommendation marked; zero turns present a corpus anchor without its inline gloss; zero example-bearing turns where two options share an outcome (EVAL-7)
